statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is moderate at 36, edging up on hardened US-Iran rhetoric while the rates and energy carry is unchanged.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z on Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly twenty hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the backdrop. Re-verification during this hour found the Friday close, VIX, the curve and crude unchanged, and one incremental change on the geopolitical side: Trump described the Strait of Hormuz as American territory and Iran's foreign ministry called new US sanctions a declaration of war, without any accompanying supply disruption or military escalation. That is rhetoric rather than transmission, so it lifts Stress by a point and leaves Tail untouched. No danger window is carried, because none can be evidenced in a closed market.
headline: Fourth consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, with Friday's cash NDX close of 29,308.86, +0.33%, re-verified as the last observed Nasdaq-100 reference.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run into Sunday's second UTC hour. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That close snapped a five-day Nasdaq-100 losing streak, though the index still ended the week about 2% lower, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell roughly 5% over the same week. VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the base of a 14.77-15.95 range. The backdrop behind Stress is a rates, energy and headline carry rather than an equity-structure one: the curve closed with the 2-year at 4.24%, the 10-year at 4.74% and the 30-year at 5.28% after touching its highest level since 2007 earlier in the week, while WTI held 87.06 and Brent 94.39 with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed. Reporting verified at this assessment put market-implied odds of a September rate hike near 35% and around 66% by December. The one incremental change against the prior hour is rhetorical: Trump described the Strait of Hormuz as American territory and Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called new US sanctions a declaration of war, with no verified military escalation or supply disruption alongside it. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is rotational rather than one-way, with index futures modestly firmer, VIX futures lower, Treasury futures softer, gold sharply higher, megacaps five-of-eight positive on wide two-sided dispersion and semiconductors mixed to weaker. None of that is live price-path evidence, and none of it establishes the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures. The week ahead carries PCE and the second GDP estimate on Wednesday, NVIDIA results after Wednesday's cash close and Jackson Hole from Thursday with Chair Warsh speaking on Friday; all remain scheduled checkpoints outside this horizon.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 18 hourly assessments are available and 6 clock-hours, all in the 21 August overnight window, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the early European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt and stayed there. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to 35 by the final available hour as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend headline risk. No danger window was published in any of those hours.

Stress eases from 36 to a 34 trough through the deep weekend hours and then climbs back to 41 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; its composition is unchanged, with the 30-year at 5.28% after a nineteen-year high earlier in the week, crude held near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse that hardened rhetorically during this hour without producing any supply or military discontinuity.
